_comment: A one-sided cap on the fraction of mutants that survive, NOT an exact-count ratchet. The pool is a seeded sample over whichever files a diff put in scope, so an exact count is not comparable between two clean branches; see the header of tests/mutation_table.py. Lower it with --record on a run whose survivors are all explained; raise it only as a deliberate, argued edit.
reason: Both caps stay OPEN at 1.0 and this is deliberate. The first real run of the changed scope (CI run 34658441338, on a runner rather than a laptop) killed 8 of 10 and is recorded in last_measured -- but 10 mutants is a sample, and a cap set at a sample's own rate reddens the next branch that happens to draw three survivors instead of two, which is the random failure this fraction exists to avoid. The nightly's 40-mutant full-package pool is the first estimate worth gating on, and mutation-nightly is on main: CI run 35395283955 drove it, its score recorded in last_measured.full. The cap still stays open because a cap moves down only on a run whose survivors are all explained (tests/mutation_table.py --record), and that run's survivors have not been triaged yet; record the cap here once they are.
